subject: Calibra Health — infra decision criteria & reserved capacity asks
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@calibrahealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Calibra Health — infra decision criteria & reserved capacity asks

Thanks again for the call earlier, Jordan — good to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (from our discovery)
- Primary workload: real-time user-facing summarization + nightly batch embedding index rebuilds.
- SLO: 95th pct latency < 250ms for short chat/generation flows, expected steady-state qps ~250 with peaks to ~750/day.
- Data security: PHI-in-scope for a subset of requests, need VPC/private deployment or customer-managed KMS.
- Decision timeline: architecture decision by end of Q3, procurement in early Q4.

What we need from you to finalize the evaluation matrix
1) Priority ranking: latency vs cost vs data isolation (one-liner).
2) Recent token volume and typical batch sizes for nightly jobs (sample numbers OK).
3) Any existing commitments with cloud vendors (reserved instances, marketplace contracts).

Proposed next tests (what Redwood can run / colleagues to coordinate)
- Dedicated vs hyperscaler smoke: 2-week throughput/latency run (real workload replay) on a reserved pool vs comparable public cloud GPUs.
- Failure/scale rehearsal: simulate 20% pod loss and observe graceful fallback to smaller model variant.
- Cost-run: run 48-hour steady-state to estimate per-10k-token cost at current batching settings.

Attachments: Calibra-MAP.xlsx (your mutual action plan template) — I attached a filled draft for your edits. Also attached a short capacity-benchmark-plan.pdf with test definitions.

Next steps / asks (short)
- Could you confirm priority ranking by EOD Tuesday?
- Can we get a sample of the last 2 weeks of token counts (anonymized) by Wed?
- If agreeable, I’ll schedule a 2-week dedicated trial window starting the week of June 28 — Sean will scope the infra.

Thanks — OlgA

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@calibrahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Calibra Health Sales <sales@calibrahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Calibra Health — infra decision criteria & reserved capacity asks

Thanks, Olga — that recap is spot on. Quick answers inline: 

Priority ranking: latency > data isolation > cost (we can tolerate a modest premium for PHI workloads).
Token volumes: average daily tokens ~18M, peak daily ~56M; nightly batch uses ~3.2B tokens (index rebuild). I will send a CSV with anonymized hourly counts by Wed.
Vendor commitments: we have existing 1yr reserved commit with a hyperscaler (private pricing) for compute but it is scoped to GPU training and not inference; we can consider marketplace reservations if the economics are compelling.

About tests: the 2-week dedicated trial sounds perfect. Two asks from our side: 
- Can Redwood guarantee capacity during calendar windows (reserved pool) and provide runbooks for fallback?
- Will you provide a cost model mapping tokens->cost for both dedicated and hyperscaler options so we can present to procurement?

Happy to sync Tue morning to align the MA P and dates.

Jordan
Director of Product
Calibra Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Calibra Health — infra decision criteria & reserved capacity asks

FYI — Jordan confirmed priorities and token volumes inline. Key follow-ups for us: 

1) Trial scope & SLOs (owner: Sean)
- 2-week dedicated pool, target 95th <250ms for short requests, steady qps 250 with spikes to 750. Need capacity carveout and SLA behavior documented.

2) Cost modeling (owner: Evelyn)
- Produce a side-by-side per-10k-token estimate: Redwood Dedicated (reserved 3-month and 12-month tiers) vs equivalent hyperscaler marketplace instances (assume spot/bursting and reserved pricing where applicable). Include delta for PHI handling (KMS/HSM) overhead.

3) Test definitions and artifacts (owner: Olga)
- Provide replay harness + sample anonymized workload template, and the capacity-benchmark-plan.pdf we’ll run. Also include failure injection steps.

4) Timeline & procurement asks
- Jordan indicated decision by end of Q3. We should prepare a procurement pack (pricing, SOW, draft contract addendum for reserved capacity).

Attachments: capacity-benchmark-plan.pdf (see test cases).

Sean — can you confirm we have a free reserved pool week of June 28? Evelyn — can you start the topline cost model draft by Monday EOD? I’ll produce the replay harness and coordinate keys for PHI testing (customer-provided test dataset will be used in VPC).

-Olga

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@calibrahealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>, Maya Torres <maya@cloudvendor.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Calibra Health — infra decision criteria & reserved capacity asks

Jordan — thanks for the quick answers and the token numbers. Confirming next actions and what we will deliver before the trial: 

What Redwood will deliver this week
- Finalized 2-week trial runbook with exact capacity reservation windows (owner: Sean).
- Cost comparison spreadsheet: Dedicated reserved (3M / 12M commit tiers) vs hyperscaler marketplace equivalents; includes PHI handling add-on line items (owner: Evelyn).
- Replay harness + anonymized sample template + failure-injection recipe (owner: Olga).
- Procurement pack draft: pricing, SLA language, addendum for reserved capacity and KMS requirements (owner: Olga).

Trial assumptions & constraints (please confirm)
- We’ll provision a private reserved pool equivalent to ~6 x A100-class GPUs for the trial. If you need different sizing, tell us by Wed EOD.
- Redwood will provide a single-tenant VPC for PHI test traffic and will support customer-managed KMS.
- If the trial shows we meet latency and reliability SLOs, we can produce a 12-month reserved proposal with predictable throughput guarantees.

Quick asks for you
- Confirm the trial window (we proposed week of June 28).
- Share the anonymized hourly token CSV by Wed so we can seed the replay harness.
- Any scheduling constraints for your security/compliance team (we plan a short kickoff with your security on Day 0).

Attachment note: I reattached Calibra-MAP.xlsx with the proposed dates filled in.

If helpful, looping in Maya from CloudVendor to provide marketplace instance pricing so we can include exact hyperscaler SKU numbers in the cost model.

Thanks — Olga
